longForm.overview:

Where ⬛ reads as solid-black-coded circle-shape read and ⬜ reads as solid-white-coded circle-shape read, ⚪ captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate white coded circle-shape — a 'white ⚪' list-bullet marker or a 'circle-pulse pulse ⚪' list-marker reveal. The white fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern list-bullet aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as white coded rather than literal circle-shape-coded shape.

In real-world usage ⚪ lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate list-bullet energy. A partner sends it on a 'white ⚪' list-bullet marker. A friend sends it on a 'circle-pulse pulse ⚪' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'white coded ⚪' list thread. The white fill cue is what makes the emoji feel white coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'white coded circle-shape moment.'

What separates ⚪ from the rest of the shape family is the white register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). It is saying 'white coded circle-shape,' which carries a specific design-coded tradition. That is why ⚪ travels especially well on partner list-bullet markers, list-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with white energy.

Skip ⚪ when you want to communicate a different color. The white coded register is too white-coded for moments that need a literal neutral fill; use ⬛ or ⬜ when the design needs to land clean.
